title: What are the rules of the prime puzzle?
description: A filled grid has a number beside every row and below every column. The video checks the nine numbers and the six products to find the rules, and Keeko's doubt that the side numbers are sums is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the rules of the puzzle are that every cell is a prime, each row multiplies to the number at its right, and each column multiplies to the number below it. Watch for students who add the numbers in a row instead of multiplying.

source: The figure on the left shows the puzzle. The figure on the right shows the solution of the puzzle. Think what the rules can be to solve the puzzle.
video_script.why: The child checks that every number in the solved grid is a prime, multiplies each row and each column, and reads the rules from what matches.
video_script.substitution: Look at the cells, multiply each row and each column, and see what each product matches.
video_script.anchor: the solved grid with rows 5 5 3, 2 3 7 and 17 2 3, with 75, 42 and 102 at the right of the rows and 170, 30 and 63 below the columns
video_script.wrong_answer: the number beside each row is the sum of the row
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the number beside each row is the sum of the row. Five and five and three make thirteen, not seventy five, and only the product, five times five times three, gives seventy five, so the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Fill the grid with prime numbers only

final_answer.value: Fill the grid with prime numbers only so that the product of each row is the number to the right of the row and the product of each column is the number below the column
final_answer.spoken: fill the grid with prime numbers only, so that the product of each row is the number to the right of the row, and the product of each column is the number below the column

hold_back: Answer: Fill the grid with prime numbers only so that the product of each row is the number to the right of the row and the product of each column is the number below the column
never_show: the number beside each row is the sum of the row
maths_rules: the worked puzzle has rows [5,5,3], [2,3,7], [17,2,3] and row products 75, 42, 102; column products 170, 30, 63
the cells are 5, 5, 3, 2, 3, 7, 17, 2, 3; each is a prime
so the rules are: prime cells only, row product at the right, column product below
5 + 5 + 3 = 13, which is not 75, so the side numbers are not sums
video_script.design: One idea: read the rules from a solved puzzle by checking the cells, the rows and the columns. Assumes multiplication of three numbers. Wrong idea: the side numbers are sums. The solved grid stays on the board to the end.
